name: Qatar Islamic Bank
founded: 1982 (incorporated 8 July 1982 under Emiri Decree No. 45 of 1982; operations began 1983; first Islamic financial institution in Qatar)
ownership_summary: QSE-listed. At FY2025 (Annual Report 2025 governance disclosures) Qatar Investment Authority owned 16.67% and Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr Al Thani more than 6.54%; government ownership was 21.58%; 9,390 shareholders; Qatari holders 81.45%. The June 2026 results presentation shows QH (QIA) 16.4%, other domestic 65.2% and foreign 18.4% as at 30 Jun 2026.

shareholders.holder: Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr Al Thani

government_link: Yes - Qatar Investment Authority is the largest shareholder (16.67% at FY2025; 16.4% via QH at 30 Jun 2026); total government ownership 21.58% (Annual Report 2025, p.39). The bank cites 'strong Government support with the QIA as its largest shareholder' (results presentation).
group_structure: Qatar Islamic Bank (Q.P.S.C.) is the QSE-listed parent. Consolidated subsidiaries (30 Jun 2026): QIB (UK) (99.71%, London, 'investment banking' - real estate finance and private banking), Arab Finance House (Lebanon, 99.99%), Aqar Real Estate Development and Investment (49%, controlled via board majority), Durat Al Doha Real Estate (82.61%), QIB Sukuk Ltd (100%), QIB Solutions LLC (100%, IT services). Overseas branch: QIB Sudan. Associates: QInvest LLC (49%, investment bank licensed by QFCRA; reclassified from 65.62% subsidiary to associate in 2025 after a partial stake sale; profiled separately as qa-qinvest - its AUM, people and capabilities belong in that file and are equity-accounted here, so do not add), Al Jazeera Finance (30%), Damaan Islamic Insurance (18.75% at FY2025), Bawabat Al Shamal Real Estate (25%).

footprint: Qatar-centric: 22 branches in Qatar plus one branch in Sudan (30 Jun 2026 interim statements note 1); results presentation: 22 branches and offices and over 191 ATMs/CDMs in Qatar at 30 Jun 2026. International presence through QIB UK (London), Arab Finance House (Beirut) and QIB Sudan (Khartoum). Head office moved to QIB Towers, West Bay, in 2025. Second-largest bank in Qatar by total assets, financing and net profit; ~38% of listed Islamic banks' assets in Qatar (results presentation, June 2026).
customer_segments: Personal banking tiers: Essential Banking (mass), Tamayuz Banking (affluent; QAR 350k deposit or QAR 50k salary), Private Banking (by invitation/referral, HNW); youth (QIB Junior), domestic workers (QIB Lite app), university students, payroll; SME; corporate/wholesale and government; international real-estate and private-banking clients via QIB UK.
business_lines: Four reporting segments: Corporate banking, Personal banking, Group function (treasury, investment, finance), Local & international subsidiaries. Personal banking: accounts and deposits (Misk prize account, Flexi CD), personal/home/vehicle financing, cards, takaful (bancatakaful savings plans), Tamayuz and Private Banking with wealth and investment advisory, and in-app QSE stock trading via partner broker The Group Securities. Wholesale banking: corporate finance, trade, transaction banking, alternative financing. Treasury and sukuk investments. In H1 2026 Personal banking generated QAR 1,260.7m net financing/investing income and QAR 248.2m net fees (segment note).

capabilities.wealth_summary: QIB's wealth offer sits in the Personal Banking Group under GM Dorai Anand; the Annual Report 2025 org chart places a Wealth Management unit under the Chief Personal & Private Banking Officer. Tiers are Tamayuz (affluent: QAR 350k deposit, QAR 50k salary or QAR 3m financing eligibility) and Private Banking (by invitation or referral; relationship-balance criterion not quantified). Private Banking offers Shari'a-compliant sukuk, equities, structured investment products, mutual funds, FX and real estate investments, plus investment advisory and active portfolio management. All private-banking RMs are certified in international investments. Clients get video banking and portfolio monitoring in the QIB Mobile App. QIB was named Euromoney Qatar's Best Private Bank 2026. Digital investing is limited to QSE stock trading inside the QIB Mobile App through partner broker The Group Securities (launched July 2021), plus IPO services and viewing deposits and investments; the app has 320+ features. QIB has no in-house asset manager or broker: QInvest (49% associate) is the group's investment bank, and QIB UK adds London real estate finance and private banking. No wealth AUM or client numbers are disclosed.

segments.name: Tamayuz Banking
segments.eligibility: Any one of: minimum start-up and yearly average deposit QAR 350,000 for 6 months; salary credit QAR 50,000 per month; or non-salaried person eligible for financing of QAR 3 million+ with at least QAR 1.5 million annual account inflows.

segments.name: Private Banking (QIB Private)
segments.eligibility: Minimum relationship balance (deposits, investments and financed assets; amount not published), active engagement, and in select cases invitation or referral.

private_banking.detail: QIB Private (Shari'a-compliant private banking 'since 1995'). Certified RMs; a priority private banking centre at QIB Al Sadd branch; door-to-door or fully digital onboarding; multi-currency accounts and deposits; investments (sukuk, real estate, international equities, ESG-focused deposit, structured investment products, mutual funds, FX); investment advisory with active portfolio management; financing against investment portfolios; 24x7 private hotline and video banking with e-signatures. Named Qatar's Best Private Bank by Euromoney (Private Banking Awards 2026). QIB UK also runs a private banking team, under its CCO.

asset_management.detail: No in-house asset management subsidiary or proprietary fund range was found at the bank. QInvest LLC (49% associate since 2025, QFC-licensed) is the group's investment bank / asset manager and is profiled separately as qa-qinvest. The bank's only AUM line is off-balance-sheet AUM of QAR 10.5m.

brokerage.detail: Via partner, not in-house: customers with a brokerage account at The Group Securities Company and a National Investor Number link it in the QIB Mobile App ('My Products' > 'Brokerage'). They can trade QSE-listed stocks in real time, move funds instantly between bank and brokerage accounts, see net worth and portfolio, and use a single sign-on. Qatar only.

digital_investing.detail: QIB Mobile App (320+ features): in-app QSE equity trading through The Group Securities (launched 8 Jul 2021), IPO subscription services, and viewing of deposits and investments. Private Banking clients get portfolio monitoring, transactions and secure messaging/video with RMs. Tamayuz and Private customers have a dedicated interface. No in-app funds, sukuk or international equities purchase found. AI-powered features for analysing customer behaviour were added in 2025.

advisory.detail: Investment advisory and personalised wealth planning by certified Private Banking RMs; Tamayuz clients get 'expert financial recommendations' and access to sukuk and portfolio diversification in Qatar and globally.

discretionary.detail: The Private Banking page says QIB will 'actively manage your portfolio', but no discretionary mandate product, terms or manager were found.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model-portfolio offering found on the personal, Private Banking, Tamayuz or mobile-app pages or in the Annual Report 2025.

funds_platform.detail: Private Banking lists 'mutual funds' among investment opportunities, but no fund shelf, fund names or platform provider is published.

structured_products.detail: 'Structured investment products' are offered to Private Banking customers (no issuers or terms published).

private_markets.detail: Private Banking offers 'real estate investments' (Qatar and abroad via a network of projects) but no private equity, private credit or fund-based private-markets product was found. QIB UK finances prime London real estate.

islamic_wealth.detail: Fully Shari'a-compliant: sukuk, Shari'a-screened equities, structured investments, mutual funds and real estate for Private Banking; Sustainable Flexi CD; Afaq savings takaful plan; QSE trading via The Group Securities.

partners.what: QSE stock trading inside the QIB Mobile App via linked brokerage accounts, with a customised platform for QIB app users
Temenos core banking system implemented in 2016 (QIB 'our journey' timeline)
Shari'a-compliant Buy Now Pay Later in Qatar (2025)

initiatives.what: QIB Mobile App enhancements: advanced search across 320+ features, redesigned credit-card overview, in-app customer survey.
Named Qatar's Best Private Bank by Euromoney (Private Banking Awards 2026); highlights certified RMs and Private Banking video banking.
Greg Ellison (ex-Alpha Bank London, Barclays Wealth) joined as CEO of QIB UK.
Partial sale of QInvest; QInvest reclassified from 65.62% subsidiary to 49% associate.
Digital: QIB Junior App launched (ages 8-17); AI-powered features in QIB Mobile Apps; mobile banking users +12%, digital financial transactions +39% vs 2024.

opportunities: Digital investing is limited to QSE equities via a third-party broker (The Group Securities); no in-app funds, sukuk, international equities or model portfolios found, although the app has 320+ features and mobile users grew 12% in 2025 (S12, S13, S6).
Private Banking sells sukuk, international equities, structured products and mutual funds, but no fund platform or provider is named and there is no published discretionary mandate (S10, S14).
Private Banking was named Euromoney Qatar's Best Private Bank 2026, and the bank stresses digital engagement (portfolio monitoring, video banking) for HNW clients (S14).
No in-house asset manager after QInvest became a 49% associate in 2025, so the bank's own product shelf depends on third parties or the associate (S4, S8).
barriers: Fully Islamic bank: every product must be Shari'a-compliant and approved by its Shari'a supervisory board (S3 note 1.1).
Existing investment ecosystem partners: QInvest (49% associate; QIB CEO and Chairman sit on its board) and The Group Securities for brokerage (S1, S2, S12).

discrepancies.detail: Annual Report 2025 executive table lists 'Chief Wholesale Banking Officer' (Fawzi) and 'Chief Personal Banking Officer' (Anand), and its org chart shows 'Chief - Personal & Private Banking Officer'. The website and the Sep 2026 release use 'General Manager - Wholesale Banking Group' and 'General Manager - Personal Banking Group'.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the website titles (most recent, confirmed by Sep 2026 release); AR titles noted in appointed_note.
